body.statement:
Let \(A\subset\mathbb R\) be measurable and let \(\lambda\) be a finite
nonnegative measure concentrated on \(A\) for which the moments through degree
\(d\) are finite.  There exist at most \(d+1\) points \(q_j\in A\) and
positive weights \(w_j\) such that
\(\int x^k d\lambda(x)=\sum_jw_jq_j^k\) for every \(0\le k\le d\).

source.locator: Theorem 2, applied to the moment map of degrees zero through four

attestation.note: Stable primary-source handle and exact theorem location supplied; no verbatim source text is reproduced.

body.justification: This supplies finite positive nodes while preserving the prescribed open-half-line concentration set.
body.gap: This is classical cubature substrate, not a contribution of the note.
body.consumer: It permits finite inverse and fifth moments in the necessity proof and finite node unions in the common-support construction.
